stories.primary_headline: Oil companies challenge Karnataka's claim of excess ethanol in petrol, question testing methodology

primary_source.headline: Oil companies challenge Karnataka's claim of excess ethanol in petrol, question testing methodology
primary_source.content: New Delhi: State-run oil marketing companies Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL), and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL) have challenged Karnataka government's claims that petrol sold at certain outlets in the state contained 26-31 per cent ethanol, questioning the sampling and testing procedures used to arrive at the findings.The three companies said E20 petrol supplied across their retail networks, including Karnataka, conforms to the Bureau of Indian Standards' IS 17021 specifications, which prescribe an ethanol content of 19-21 per cent.In a joint statement, the oil companies said the findings cited by the Karnataka government were not supported by tests conducted in accordance with the prescribed statutory and technical procedures. They also questioned the use of third-party laboratory certificates that, they said, did not disclose sufficient details of the testing methodology to independently verify the reported ethanol levels.The dispute centres on a testing exercise conducted in October 2026 by Karnataka's Department of Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology, which claimed that petrol samples collected from certain retail outlets contained substantially higher ethanol concentrations than the prescribed limit.The OMCs said the sampling procedure mandated under the Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation of Supply, Distribution and Prevention of Malpractices) Order, 2005, read with the Marketing Discipline Guidelines (MDG) 2024, requires six one-litre samples to be collected.Of these, two samples must be handed over to the dealer against acknowledgement, two retained by the oil company or department, and two sent to a laboratory specified under the control order. Sample labels must be jointly signed, with test results communicated to the dealer and oil company within the prescribed timeframe.While samples collected during a September exercise were routed through the State Level Coordinator to designated OMC laboratories, the companies said the subsequent October sampling was conducted without their representatives.They said they had not received the corresponding retention samples, outlet-wise details or laboratory reports despite seeking them through the state-level coordinator, denying them and the dealers an opportunity to independently verify the findings or seek retesting.The companies also questioned the testing methodology cited in the laboratory certificates. Under IS 17021:2018, as amended in August 2025, ethanol content in E20 petrol must be determined through specified methods, including Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy, water extraction or gas chromatography under prescribed ASTM standards.Where gas chromatography is used, the standard requires the sample to be diluted in a 1:1 ratio with oxygenate-free petrol and the result corrected against an E10 certified reference material.The Karnataka certificates, however, merely mentioned ethanol percentage determined through gas chromatography without specifying the applicable test standard, dilution procedure or reference material used, the OMCs said.They argued that the reported ethanol levels of 26-31 per cent could not be independently validated without these details.The companies also flagged discrepancies in the density readings. The certificates reportedly showed densities of 0.742-0.749 grams per cubic centimetre for samples claimed to contain 26-31 per cent ethanol, against 0.752-0.760 grams per cubic centimetre recorded in E20 samples tested by the OMCs.Since ethanol has a higher density than petrol, a higher ethanol concentration would ordinarily be expected to increase the density of the blend, they said, adding that the discrepancy warranted verification using prescribed testing methods and reference samples.Seeking to counter the Karnataka findings, the companies cited a nationwide quality-monitoring exercise conducted by the OMCs and the Centre for High Technology (CHT), under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.Up to 31.2% ethanol in petrol: Karnataka govt alleges oil companies sell blends exceeding prescribed limitsUnder the OMC/CHT Quality Coordination Cell exercise, 893 E20 samples collected from depots and retail outlets of the three companies across 27 states and Union Territories were tested at refinery and OMC quality-control laboratories.All 893 samples were found to contain ethanol within the prescribed 19-21 per cent range, according to the companies.The results included 56 samples from Karnataka, drawn from different locations and covering all three OMCs. These recorded ethanol content of 19-20 per cent, averaging 19.30 per cent, they said.The companies said ethanol blending at refineries and depots was carried out through calibrated and automated proportioning systems, with quality-control protocols governing the process. Blending was not a manual or arbitrary exercise, they added.The companies also questioned estimates cited in the Karnataka controversy that E20 fuel could result in annual consumer mileage losses of around Rs 62,000 crore and vehicle repair expenses of Rs 39,000 crore, taking the combined impact to approximately Rs 1.01 lakh crore.They said such estimates required scientific substantiation and could not be based on a blanket assumption of 10 per cent mileage loss across the country's vehicle population.More than 30 crore two-wheelers and 4 crore four-wheelers have been running on E20 fuel for over three years, while more than 6 crore people visit petrol pumps daily, the companies said.They argued that the absence of any reported widespread vehicle breakdowns was an important consideration in assessing concerns over fuel quality and vehicle performance.Citing the Petroleum Ministry's August 12, 2025 response on ethanol blending, the OMCs said studies involving the Inter-Ministerial Committee, Indian Oil, the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) and the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM) had examined the performance implications of E20.Vehicles calibrated for E20 could experience mileage reductions of around 1-2 per cent, while certain other vehicles could see declines of 3-6 per cent, depending on vehicle category and calibration, according to the ministry's assessment.The companies said the Rs 39,000 crore estimate for vehicle repairs also needed to be supported by actual vehicle-performance data, materials compatibility studies and documented repair costs.India's ethanol-blending programme, which began with a pilot initiative in 2001, is aimed at reducing dependence on imported crude oil, strengthening domestic agricultural value chains and improving energy security.The programme has been expanded through successive policy interventions, including the National Policy on Biofuels, 2018, and the NITI Aayog roadmap for ethanol blending.According to Petroleum Ministry data cited by the OMCs, the programme since the 2014-15 ethanol supply year has generated foreign exchange savings of more than Rs 1.97 lakh crore, substituted approximately 316 lakh metric tonnes of crude oil, reduced carbon dioxide emissions by around 952 lakh metric tonnes and resulted in payments of more than Rs 1.66 lakh crore to farmers.During the 2025-26 ethanol supply year, which ended on October 31, 2026, the three public sector OMCs procured 1,089 crore litres of ethanol and blended 1,134 crore litres against petrol sales of approximately 5,673 crore litres, the statement said.The companies also rejected suggestions that they had a commercial incentive to blend ethanol beyond prescribed levels, arguing that additional ethanol procurement would increase their costs.The three OMCs have asked the Karnataka government to share complete sampling documentation, outlet-wise laboratory reports and details of the testing methodology used to arrive at the reported findings.They have also sought access to the counterpart samples for independent testing at an authorised laboratory using the prescribed referee method, in the presence of representatives of both the state government and the oil companies.The companies said they were willing to participate in joint sampling and testing in accordance with the Control Order and MDG 2024, adding that any deviation established through the prescribed procedure would be dealt with under applicable guidelines.

According to reports, Microsoft opted not to renew the contract as the rented capacity no longer aligned with its evolving technical requirements and internal scaling goals. This decision follows a broader reassessment of Microsoft’s multi-billion dollar cloud partnerships as the company prioritizes proprietary hardware and internal data center expansion to support its AI ambitions. brief_bullets: The U.S. labor market demonstrated unexpected resilience in October, adding 165,000 nonfarm payroll jobs and surpassing analyst forecasts. This growth, bolstered by upward revisions to the previous two months, pushed the national unemployment rate down to 4.1 percent. Economists, including Claudia Sahm of New Century Advisors, view these figures as a clear indicator of sustained economic expansion despite broader concerns regarding wage moderation. By outperforming expectations, the report underscores the underlying strength of the American workforce, providing a robust buffer against potential cooling trends and reinforcing the narrative of a durable, high-performing economy that continues to defy pessimistic projections regarding long-term labor market stability.
why_it_matters_bullets: Stronger-than-expected job growth signals economic resilience, potentially influencing Federal Reserve interest rate policy and long-term market stability.

stories.primary_headline: 'Don't confuse PM Modi, convince him for open debate with me': Rahul Gandhi tells Amit Shah

primary_source.headline: 'Don't confuse PM Modi, convince him for open debate with me': Rahul Gandhi tells Amit Shah
primary_source.content:
New Delhi: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday said Home Minister Amit Shah should not confuse Prime Minister Narendra Modi and instead should convince the PM to have an open debate with him on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Gandhi shared a video montage contrasting Shah's remarks in Parliament in December last year that a debate on the SIR of electoral rolls cannot take place in the two Houses with his comments on Thursday that the government is open to convening a special session of Parliament to discuss the SIR.In a post in Hindi, Gandhi said, "Amit Shah ji, don't confuse Modi ji. Just convince him to have an open debate with me. Any platform, any time.""Daro Mat (Do not be scared)," the leader of opposition (LoP) in the Lok Sabha said.अमित शाह जी, मोदी जी को कन्फ़्यूज़ मत कीजिए।बस उन्हें मेरे साथ खुली बहस के लिए मना लीजिए। कोई भी मंच, कोई भी समय।डरो मत। pic.twitter.com/TciYEtNBIt&mdash; Rahul Gandhi (@RahulGandhi) November 6, 2026
 

Tagging Gandhi's post, Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh also took a dig at Modi."The PM can also use a teleprompter," he said.प्रधानमंत्री जी टेलीप्रॉम्प्टर का इस्तेमाल भी कर सकते हैं। https://t.co/XOyyFthUJ4&mdash; Jairam Ramesh (@Jairam_Ramesh) November 6, 2026
 

Gandhi has been repeatedly daring Prime Minister Modi to debate with him openly. The former Congress president has "guaranteed" that it would be proven in five minutes that the PM was a traitor."Let's debate right there on Adani ji's NDTV, Mr Modi. The platform is yours, the judge is yours too -- be it Adani ji or Mohan Bhagwat ji.""I guarantee it -- I'll prove in just 5 minutes that Narendra Modi is a 'deshdrohi' (traitor)," Gandhi said in a post in Hindi on X on Wednesday.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge has also said the prime minister should come forward and face the questions on vote theft that the nation was posing.The BJP leaders have scoffed at Gandhi's challenge. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said that while Gandhi is asking the PM to choose the venue for a debate, there already exists one in Parliament and reminded him that he happens to be the LoP in the Lok Sabha and needs to show some seriousness and responsibility.Earlier on Tuesday, Gandhi had challenged Modi to an open debate on his charge that the "opposition is anti-national" and asked why the prime minister has not filed a defamation case against him over his "foreign connections" allegation.He had accused Modi of occupying the PM's chair with "foreign help", within a day of his earlier challenge for an open debate with the prime minister for accusing the opposition of taking foreign help to destabilise the country.

primary_source.content: Once the deal is signed by both sides and the formalities are completed, it should take effect in January 2027. The Indian universities, research institutions, companies and scientists can now use the funding of the programme and work on projects with European partners.

sources.headline: India Set to Join EU's 93.5 Billion Euro Horizon Europe Research Program
India, EU conclude multi-billion Euro global innovation programme

brief_bullets: India and the European Union have successfully concluded negotiations for New Delhi to join the 93.5 billion euro Horizon Europe research and innovation program, effective January 2027. Led by the European Commission and Indian authorities, this agreement enables Indian universities, enterprises, and scientists to access direct funding and co-lead collaborative projects under Pillar II alongside European counterparts. This landmark scientific pact strengthens bilateral ties ahead of a forthcoming free trade agreement, cementing a comprehensive strategic agenda focused on tackling critical global challenges including health, climate change, and advanced digital technologies.
why_it_matters_bullets: It institutionalizes deep technological integration between India and Europe, accelerating joint innovations in critical global sectors.

Airstrikes on market in southwestern Yemen kill at least 30, Houthis say

brief_bullets: Airstrikes targeting a crowded market in the al-Waziyah district of Yemen's southwestern Taiz province have resulted in the deaths of at least 20 people and left 15 others wounded, according to statements by Houthi Health Ministry spokesperson Anees Alsabahi on the Houthi-run television network Al Masirah. The tragic incident underscores the ongoing devastation facing civilians amid the prolonged Yemeni conflict, intensifying humanitarian concerns as military operations continue to impact densely populated commercial areas. While attribution for the strikes remains under intense scrutiny given the fractured nature of the regional war, the high civilian death toll highlights the severe risks noncombatants face as violence persists.
why_it_matters_bullets: The deadly market strikes escalate regional tensions and deepen the catastrophic humanitarian crisis affecting Yemeni civilians.

stories.primary_headline: 'What About Haryana?' Punjab Minister's Retort On Delhi Pollution Blame

primary_source.headline: 'What About Haryana?' Punjab Minister's Retort On Delhi Pollution Blame
primary_source.content: Punjab Finance Minister questions BJP's focus on AAP-ruled Punjab as Delhi's AQI nears 'severe'; BJP MP Manoj Tiwari asks if farm fires are a "conspiracy to ruin Diwali"

sources.headline: 'What About Haryana?' Punjab Minister's Retort On Delhi Pollution Blame
82-yr-old claim, 30-yr court battle: SC settles Bhakra-Beas power dispute between HP, Punjab, Haryana - ThePrint

brief_bullets: As Delhi’s air quality index approaches severe levels, Punjab Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema has challenged the BJP’s singular focus on AAP-governed Punjab regarding farm fires, questioning the lack of scrutiny toward neighboring Haryana. This political friction intensified after BJP MP Manoj Tiwari suggested that the persistent stubble burning might be a deliberate conspiracy to disrupt Diwali festivities. Simultaneously, the Supreme Court has finally resolved a long-standing thirty-year legal dispute between Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, and Haryana concerning the Bhakra-Beas power-sharing agreement. These developments highlight the complex intersection of regional environmental accountability, escalating political polarization between the AAP and BJP, and the ongoing struggle to manage inter-state resource distribution amidst a worsening public health crisis in the national capital region.
why_it_matters_bullets: Persistent inter-state political blame-shifting undermines coordinated regional policy, exacerbating the public health crisis caused by seasonal air pollution.

sources.headline: Gold drops 1% as strong US payrolls boost dollar, yields - Reuters
Gold Extends Drop on Stronger-Than-Expected US Employment Data

brief_bullets: Gold prices retreated by 1% following a robust U.S. nonfarm payrolls report, which signaled unexpected strength in the labor market. This economic data bolstered the U.S. dollar and pushed Treasury yields higher, diminishing the appeal of non-yielding bullion among investors. Market participants now anticipate that the Federal Reserve may maintain a hawkish monetary policy stance, potentially implementing further interest rate hikes to aggressively combat persistent inflationary pressures. Consequently, the precious metal faces renewed downward pressure as capital shifts toward higher-yielding assets, reflecting broader market uncertainty regarding the central bank's future trajectory in balancing economic growth against price stability.
why_it_matters_bullets: Strong labor data forces a hawkish Fed pivot, strengthening the dollar and suppressing gold as a safe-haven asset.

brief_bullets: Multi-strategy hedge fund Walleye Capital is returning approximately $2 billion to investors as it significantly scales back its equities trading operations. This strategic pivot follows a period of heightened market volatility triggered by shifting expectations regarding artificial intelligence growth and Federal Reserve interest rate policy. By downsizing its stock-focused portfolio, the firm aims to recalibrate its capital allocation amid a complex macroeconomic environment characterized by persistent inflation concerns and fluctuating chipmaker valuations. This decision reflects a broader trend among institutional managers who are increasingly cautious about maintaining large-scale equity exposure during periods of intense monetary tightening and sector-specific uncertainty, ultimately signaling a tactical retreat to preserve liquidity and mitigate risk in an unpredictable financial landscape.
why_it_matters_bullets: The capital return signals a defensive shift in hedge fund strategies amid ongoing macroeconomic volatility and interest rate uncertainty.

stories.primary_headline: Minister raises concern over rising number of maternal deaths

primary_source.headline: Minister raises concern over rising number of maternal deaths
primary_source.content: Chitradurga: The rising number of maternal deaths despite the availability of modern facilities in hospitals is a matter of concern as maternal and infant mortality can be reduced if medical officers closely monitor the health of pregnant women, Health and Minority Welfare Minister U T Khader said.He was speaking at a progress review meeting of the health and minority welfare departments held at the deputy commissioner's office auditorium on Friday.Kannada vocabulary, dialects, folk knowledge and literary heritage must be preserved: Minister UT KhaderEven if pregnant women show minor signs of complications, they should immediately be shifted to the district hospital by ambulance. They should be admitted to hospitals at least three days before delivery. Doctors should ensure the health of both mother and child during childbirth. If serious complications arise, they should be referred to the district hospital. Awareness programmes must also be conducted in rural areas, he said.Four maternal deaths have been reported in the current year. The women died due to high blood pressure and lung infections. Compared to last year, the maternal mortality rate in the district has declined by 50%, District Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) Officer D M Abhinav said.Khata campaign sees 11,000 visitors in four weeks'Visit PHCs'The minister directed taluk health officers to visit and inspect primary health centres under their jurisdiction at least three times a month.During every visit, officers should identify deficiencies and problems and take steps to address them and introduce necessary improvements, he said.Meetings involving local MLAs, organisations and hospital staff should be held at least once a month. Hospitals should not have to wait for government funds for renovation, cleaning of toilets or painting. It is the responsibility of taluk health officers to seek assistance from local MLAs and organisations to renovate and maintain hospitals, he said.Minority schoolsResidential schools and colleges under the Minority Welfare Department should give importance to sports and extracurricular activities alongside quality education. It was encouraging that SSLC results in the district's APJ Abdul Kalam, Morarji Desai and Maulana Azad residential schools had exceeded 90%, he said.MLA K C Veerendra, Urban Development Authority chairperson M K Tajpeer, Deputy Commissioner S Ramya, Assistant Commissioner K Kantaraj, Health Department district nodal officer Ranganath, District Health Officer M C Sunil Kumar, District Guarantee Schemes Implementation Authority chairperson R Shivanna, and vice-chairperson D N Mailarappa, were present.Process e-khata applications in two days, open 10 PSK-style centres in Bengaluru: D K ShivakumarOutside prescriptionsIn another progress review meeting held at the Hiriyur City Municipal Council hall on Friday, Health Minister U T Khader warned government hospital doctors of strict action if they prescribe medicines that patients are required to purchase from outside."The government is supplying all necessary medicines to patients. Asking them to buy medicines from outside amounts to exploiting the poor. This should not continue," he warned.

sources.headline: Minister raises concern over rising number of maternal deaths

brief_bullets: Karnataka Health Minister U.T. Khader has expressed urgent concern over persistent maternal mortality rates in Chitradurga, despite the availability of modern medical infrastructure. During a departmental review, the Minister mandated that medical officers proactively monitor high-risk pregnancies, facilitate early hospital admissions, and ensure timely referrals to district facilities to mitigate complications like hypertension and infections. While local officials reported a 50 percent decline in maternal deaths compared to the previous year, Khader emphasized that further progress requires rigorous oversight of primary health centers and increased community awareness. He further warned government doctors against prescribing external medications, signaling a broader push for improved accountability and administrative efficiency within the state's public healthcare delivery system.
why_it_matters_bullets: Improving maternal health outcomes is critical for public trust and reflects the state's capacity to manage essential services.

stories.primary_headline: Zelenskyy says Ukraine is continuing attacks on Russia's oil refining sector

primary_source.headline: Zelenskyy says Ukraine is continuing attacks on Russia's oil refining sector
primary_source.content: Ukraine is continuing to launch attacks on targets associated with Russia's oil sector in response to Russian strikes on energy targets, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Friday."The operation against the Russian oil refining sector is continuing -- in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy facilities," Zelenskyy said on Telegram.Russian officials reported several strikes on its oil industry targets in the past week without Ukrainian officials specifically claiming responsibility for them.

sources.headline: Zelenskyy says Ukraine is continuing attacks on Russia's oil refining sector

brief_bullets: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed that military forces are actively targeting Russia's oil refining infrastructure in direct retaliation for sustained Russian bombardments against Ukraine's domestic energy grid. This ongoing campaign of strategic strikes highlights Kyiv's asymmetric capability to project force deep inside Russian territory, impacting key economic and logistical nodes. Despite official restraint regarding specific tactical claims, Russian authorities have reported multiple recent incidents hitting domestic energy assets over the past week. The escalation marks a critical intensification of the energy war, directly threatening Moscow's refined petroleum output and state revenues.
why_it_matters_bullets: These retaliatory strikes systematically degrade Russia's critical energy infrastructure and disrupt vital petroleum export revenues.

stories.primary_headline: If Dune is this generation’s Star Wars, we are all in big trouble

primary_source.headline: If Dune is this generation’s Star Wars, we are all in big trouble
primary_source.content: According to Florence Pugh, Denis Villeneuve’s stunningly strange and breathtaking universe is the equivalent to George Lucas’ heroic space opera. Let’s hope notA long time ago, far far away, in a galaxy called the 1970s, kids dreamed of joining the rebellion, rescuing a princess and blowing up the Death Star. Peer into the cosmic tea leaves and it would become immediately clear that no amount of evildoing could withstand a neurotic gold butler, a dustbin with ideas above its station and a walking seven-foot tall shagpile carpet with a very low tolerance for disagreement.It is worth remembering this when considering Florence Pugh’s recent declaration, ahead of next month’s Dune: Part Three, that Dune is her generation’s Star Wars. And then wondering how much trouble we might be in if she’s actually right. “I think they brought back movie-going. What an event the second [Dune] was,” Pugh cheerfully told the New York Times. “It was just so lovely to be a part of something that we know is our generational kind of Star Wars.” Continue reading...
